strengths: Novel problem formulation addressing a genuine gap: autoregressive interactive LiDAR generation with single-frame input, which existing generation methods (single-frame only) and prediction methods (deterministic, multi-frame input) cannot handle

Strong experimental results demonstrating substantial improvements over baselines across multiple metrics (Chamfer Distance, MMD, JSD, L1 Error, Absrel), with particularly impressive long-horizon performance

Well-designed technical approach combining spherical projection, LDM with multi-condition control, and two complementary modules (SDE and NM) that are technically sound and properly address spatial/temporal consistency challenges
Establishment of a new benchmark protocol for long-horizon LiDAR generation evaluation (176 scenes from nuScenes) that will benefit future research
Demonstrates practical interactivity with frame-by-frame generation enabling object-level editing and control for closed-loop simulation
Clear presentation with effective figures and well-structured description of the methodology
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (spherical projection, LDM, diffusion forcing) rather than introducing fundamentally new methods; SDE is essentially nearest-neighbor matching, NM borrows directly from prior work

Critical practical limitation—requires ground truth 3D bounding boxes at inference time, severely limiting real-world applicability. Absolutely no analysis of robustness to noisy/imperfect bounding box predictions, which is essential for deployment in autonomous driving where detection errors propagate

Unfair comparison with prediction baselines: (1) uses different amounts of input information (1 frame + GT boxes vs. 6 historical frames), (2) 4D-Occ not designed for this task, (3) dramatic improvements may partly stem from ground truth conditioning that baselines don't leverage

Small and limited benchmark with only 176 valid scenes on single dataset (nuScenes). No cross-dataset validation (Waymo, KITTI), only 32-beam LiDAR, limited geographic scope. Insufficient to establish robust benchmark generalization

Incomplete evaluation lacking several critical analyses: (1) no temporal consistency metrics between frames, (2) no perceptual quality assessment, (3) no inference time or computational cost analysis, (4) no failure case or out-of-distribution evaluation, (5) no sensitivity analysis for noise schedule parameter N in NM module

SDE module design issues: nearest-neighbor matching is simplistic and doesn't handle complex occlusions; background estimation using only rotation assumes static background which is unrealistic for dynamic scenes
Missing robustness analysis: no experiments with perturbed bounding boxes, no evaluation of handling object appearance/disappearance, no analysis of what SDE learns beyond simple mask information
Reproducibility concerns: limited training details, VAE initialization not specified, hyperparameter justification incomplete, no mention of code availability

strengths: Well-motivated problem: Clearly articulates the gap between single-frame generation and multi-frame prediction methods; autoregressive approach with single-frame initiation is practical for closed-loop simulation
Strong empirical results: Substantially outperforms baselines on multiple metrics (Chamfer Distance 2.66 vs 5.06 m²; depth L1 error 0.41 vs 4.42m), with consistent improvements across time horizons
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple metrics (MMD, JSD, Chamfer Distance, ray-based depth errors), ablation studies, and qualitative demonstrations of interactive editing capabilities
Practical interactivity: Demonstrates object-level editing (moving/removing objects) with proper occlusion handling, a genuine advantage for simulation applications
New benchmark contribution: nuScenes-based evaluation protocol for long-horizon generation could be valuable for future research, despite limited scale
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Core contribution is engineering integration of existing techniques (LDM, spherical projection, FiLM, cross-attention). SDE module reduces to heuristic nearest-neighbor bounding box matching without principled justification. NM module simply adds Gaussian noise—trivial technically and lacks noise schedule justification

Unfair baseline comparison: Prediction baselines receive only multi-frame point clouds; LaGen receives privileged 3D bounding box information for object localization and identification. Fundamental input difference undermines the comparison fairness. No ablation removing bounding box conditioning

SDE module concerns: Background estimation via rotation-only transformation (Eq. 10) oversimplifies ego motion effects. Nearest-neighbor matching lacks robustness analysis for edge cases (object entry/exit, multiple same-category objects). Modest empirical improvements (2-5%, sometimes degradation at 9.5s)

NM module lacks justification: Noise schedule undefined (uniform over [0,N]? Why?). Claim that noise 'reduces over-reliance' lacks theoretical grounding. Train-inference mismatch explanation intuitive but not rigorously validated. Only 4% improvement at 9.5s

Small and unvalidated benchmark: Only 176 scenes after filtering—limited scale for establishing a benchmark. No sensitivity analysis of filtering criteria or comparison with alternative evaluation protocols

Incomplete evaluation: Chamfer Distance insensitive to perceptual quality; ray-based metrics are 1D projections. No perceptual/semantic quality evaluation, failure mode analysis, or error accumulation patterns. Interactivity evaluated only qualitatively

Generalization concerns: All experiments on nuScenes only. No evaluation on KITTI, Argoverse, or Waymo. Single LiDAR configuration (32-beam) tested. No robustness to challenging conditions (night, rain, occlusions)

Reproducibility issues: Hyperparameter choices poorly justified. Architecture details incomplete (FPN, U-Net specifics, training schedule). No mention of code release. Redundant figures (2 and 3) with unclear distinctions

Missing ablations and analyses: No ablation removing bounding box information. No simpler baseline comparisons (motion extrapolation). No computational cost analysis. No sensitivity to bounding box noise. Limited mechanistic understanding of what model learns vs. what conditioning provides

strengths: Novel problem formulation: First framework enabling frame-by-frame autoregressive LiDAR generation from single-frame input, addressing genuine gap between single-frame generation and multi-frame prediction methods
Strong quantitative results: Achieves 2-8× improvement over baselines across temporal horizons (CD of 2.66 at 9.5s vs 21.08 for 4D-Occ), demonstrating significant practical advantage

Well-designed technical contributions: SDE module provides object-level point cloud estimates better than mask-only conditioning; NM module principally addresses train-inference mismatch in autoregressive generation
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple metrics (Chamfer Distance, L1 Error, Absrel, MMD, JSD), ablation studies, qualitative results, and interactive editing demonstration
Unique interactive generation capability: Ability to edit object positions mid-generation enables diverse scenario exploration not possible with deterministic prediction methods
Clear presentation and complete framework: Well-structured paper with informative figures, complete experimental setup, and thorough methodology description
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty in components: Range images, latent diffusion models, and noise perturbation are standard techniques; core novelty is primarily problem formulation rather than algorithmic innovation
Small evaluation benchmark: Only 176 valid scenes after filtering (out of 1,000 nuScenes sequences); newly constructed benchmark has limited prior validation and may bias toward simpler scenarios

Unrealistic ground truth assumption: Method assumes perfect 3D bounding boxes at each step; no experiments with noisy/missing boxes despite this being critical in practice; significantly limits real-world applicability

Incomplete error accumulation mitigation: Even with NM module, errors accumulate (8% improvement at 6s, 16% at 9.5s in Table 5); error accumulation problem not fundamentally solved, only partially mitigated

SDE module failure modes not addressed: Nearest neighbor matching can fail in crowded scenes; background estimation doesn't handle appearance/disappearance of occluded surfaces; no failure case analysis provided
Missing key practical analyses: No computational cost comparison; no robustness to imperfect inputs; no downstream task evaluation; no generalization study across LiDAR configurations or datasets
Limited scope of evaluation: Single-dataset evaluation (nuScenes only); no cross-dataset validation; unclear generalization to 64/128-beam LiDAR or other autonomous driving benchmarks
Insufficient ablation studies: No ablation on noise schedule (critical NM component); no sensitivity analysis for SDE matching; no study of generation diversity across random seeds

strengths: Novel first-to-address contribution: autoregressive interactive LiDAR generation with frame-by-frame generation capability, addressing clear limitations of prior single-frame or trajectory-constrained methods
Sound technical design: Well-motivated SDE module leveraging bounding box information for scene decomposition and theoretically-justified NM module for error accumulation mitigation

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple datasets, diverse metrics, thorough ablation studies (Tables 7-9) demonstrating component contributions, and downstream task validation showing practical value
Interactive generation capability demonstrated with object-level editing (Figure 7) enabling scenario diversity for simulation
Practical range-view representation with corrected spherical projection accounting for multi-layer LiDAR systems
Clear presentation with well-organized supplementary material including detailed algorithms and theoretical analyses
weaknesses: Severely restricted to single-return spinning mechanical LiDAR, failing to support multi-return or emerging solid-state LiDAR systems, significantly limiting practical deployment applicability
Long-horizon generation under-evaluated despite being a key claimed contribution: main quantitative results focus on short horizons (Table 5 maximum 9.5s), error accumulation analysis lacks depth
Trajectory dependency not fully addressed: assumes known future trajectories but in closed-loop driving this depends on perception outputs, creating problematic circular dependency
Computational efficiency insufficiently analyzed: inference time 0.31-1.44s with unclear denoising step selection, training requiring 23 GPU-hours, no inference time comparison with baselines
Scene decoupling limitations: assumes accurate bounding boxes (robustness only modest), assumes rigid motion (fails for articulated objects), nearest-distance matching fails in crowded scenes
Limited generalization: evaluation on only two similar datasets, no cross-dataset or domain transfer analysis, environmental diversity not explored
Incomplete baseline comparisons: some methods designed for different tasks, recent 4D scene generation methods missing, fairness of multi-frame vs. single-frame comparison arguable
Interactive generation under-evaluated: only qualitative results in Figure 7, no quantitative metrics, limited to simple edits, lacks user validation of practical utility
Theoretical justifications with unjustified assumptions: Appendix E noise analysis assumes small noise regime; Appendix F SDE analysis assumes conditional independence not always valid

Missing technical analysis: no hyperparameter sensitivity study, minimal failure case discussion, improvement from corrected range projection (Appendix D) not quantified, partial input robustness not addressed

strengths: Addresses a relevant problem of long-horizon LiDAR scene generation for autonomous driving applications with useful interactive editing capabilities
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across two datasets (nuScenes, KITTI-360) with multiple metrics and ablation studies on individual components
Well-executed system design that integrates multiple technical components (conditional encoding, scene decomposition, noise modulation) into a working framework
Demonstrates practical utility through interactive generation with object-level control demonstrated in Figure 7
Code availability promised, potentially enabling future research
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: The approach combines existing techniques (LDM, range image projection, standard scene decomposition) without significant algorithmic innovation; each component is well-known and the contribution is primarily engineering-level integration
Misleading framing of 'autoregressive' contribution: System only uses autoregressive temporal frame generation, not point-level autoregression within frames; this overstates the conceptual novelty
Marginal empirical improvements: Tables 1-2 show often modest gains over baselines (frequently 1-5%), insufficient to justify added system complexity

Weak and dated baselines: Primary comparisons against 2021-2022 methods (LiDARGen, LiDM, RangeLDM); missing recent diffusion-based and temporal consistency methods; no comparison with concurrent video generation approaches

Scene Decoupling Estimation (SDE) module is overly simplistic: Essentially standard bounding-box-based masking with nearest-neighbor matching; the theoretical contribution (Appendix F) is straightforward linear operator decomposition without novel insights
Noise Modulation (NM) module lacks novelty: Reduces to adding scaled Gaussian noise; theoretical analysis (Appendix E) is basic Taylor expansion with marginal empirical gains in Table 8 (often <2%)

Incomplete evaluation of key claims: Interactive generation capability shown only qualitatively without quantitative metrics, user studies, or baseline comparisons; 'long-horizon' claims not fully validated (evaluation limited to ≤9.5s horizons)

Unfocused presentation: Paper attempts to cover too many aspects (single-frame, long-horizon, interactivity, temporal consistency) making the core contribution unclear; tries to be both a generation and simulation paper
Acknowledged but unresolved practical limitations: Cannot handle multi-return LiDAR; SDE's search mechanism admitted to fail in crowded scenes; no proposed solutions provided

Missing critical comparisons and analyses: No computational cost analysis, inference time evaluation, user studies for interactive generation, or failure case analysis; range image design choices unexplored

strengths: First autoregressive framework for long-horizon LiDAR generation with interactive capability, addressing a genuine gap in prior work that was limited to single-frame generation
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple datasets (nuScenes, KITTI-360) with diverse metrics, strong baselines, and thorough ablation studies demonstrating consistent improvements

Well-motivated technical components: Scene Decoupling Estimation effectively separates dynamic/static content, and Noise Modulation is grounded in theoretical analysis showing regularization of Jacobian-based error dynamics
Interactive editing capability (moving/removing objects during generation) adds significant practical value for scenario synthesis and closed-loop simulation
Strong empirical results: substantial improvements on MMD/JSD (Tables 1-2), temporal consistency metrics (Table 5), and downstream object detection (Tables 3-4)
Theoretical grounding provided in appendices with rigorous analysis of error accumulation dynamics and scene decomposition principles
Excellent presentation with clear visualizations, comprehensive supplementary material, and effective communication of complex spatiotemporal generation concepts
weaknesses: Limited novelty in individual technical components: Scene Decoupling is relatively straightforward decomposition via bounding boxes; Noise Modulation is simple Gaussian noise injection; primary novelty lies in combination rather than fundamental methodological advances

Critical dependency on accurate 3D bounding box information from previous frames for scene decomposition; robustness to detection errors not thoroughly analyzed, risking error accumulation in real deployments
Narrow domain scope limited to single-return mechanical LiDAR; explicitly doesn't model multi-return sensors or other configurations, reducing generalizability to diverse autonomous systems
Noise Modulation module shows only incremental empirical improvements (Tables 7-8) relative to complexity, with Scene Decoupling appearing more critical for performance gains

Computational cost incompletely addressed: requires 50 denoising steps for inference and 176,000 optimization steps for training, but latency analysis missing and real-time applicability for autonomous driving unclear

Evaluation primarily distribution-based (MMD, JSD, Chamfer Distance) rather than task-centric; limited downstream validation beyond object detection, missing trajectory prediction or motion planning utility assessment
Limited analysis of failure modes and error accumulation patterns; acknowledged limitations in crowded scenes due to nearest-distance matching, but not empirically validated or deeply addressed

Interactive generation constrained by simple nearest-distance-based object matching across frames; acknowledged inefficiency in crowded scenes with multiple identical categories could limit practical urban deployment
